verdict: The seam holds. All 16 acceptance criteria pass under execution, not just inspection: node --check passes on both files; transport.bridge.js exports exactly {NULL_BRIDGE, bridge, bridgeReady, esc, fmtNum}; a programmatic diff of Object.keys(NULL_BRIDGE) against the 35 keys of window.MythicTransportBridge as actually built in index.html:207827-208053 comes back empty in both directions; bridge() duck-types typeof b.signedIn === 'function' inside try/catch and never returns null; every mutator on NULL_BRIDGE (spendGems, addGems, spendRes, addRes, refundRes, setRigField, save) returns false with the measured reason written above it. Imported with no bridge the module registers window.MythicTransport, warns EXACTLY once, and every mutating entry point returns {ok:false, why} — verified by running it. Imported with a mock bridge and a stub DOM it injects mt-css once (id-guarded), builds the pinned view, and renders 2,923 chars of data-mt-stamped markup with no fallback path taken. The grep for bare globals returns comments and NULL_BRIDGE property names only; there is no .from(/.rpc(, no discord/webhook/upload token, nothing that touches _convoyCanSend, and no economy number outside b.opEcon('transport'). It clears the bar it was measured against: community.bridge.js's NULL_BRIDGE ships addGems: () => {} and saveProfile: () => {} — silent success in front of a spend, which the rubric names as a failure — and this file refuses instead and costs the alternative in the comment. The interop with the five sibling modules is real rather than assumed: dispatch(q), createCompany({name}), registerRig(vid, opts) and tariffCap(array) all land on tolerant arms that were written for exactly these call shapes, and registerRig genuinely reads opts.runsCap, so the file's loudest claim (runs_cap is the caller's to supply) is enforced and not merely asserted.
biggest_gap: Systematic stale line-number citations into index.html and the sibling modules. Every one of the six index.html anchors in index.js is wrong (_opAfterFound cited at 79968/82273/82388, actually 79986/82477/82603; `if (!_pp.owned)` cited at ~80217, actually 80239; wfBuyBoat('skiff') at ~80205, actually 80227; _transportGrantStarterRig at ~80489, actually 80450), as are five of the seven in transport.bridge.js (MythicCityBridge ~207415 → 207696; MythicTradeBridge resources ~207371 → 207654; the swallowed-save postmortem ~207446 → 207728; the boolean-mutator banner ~207358 → 207639; _garageRig ~164225 → 164461), plus depot.render.js:601/:645 → 686/723 and contracts.js:845/:685/:946-952. The claims are all substantively TRUE — the anchors exist and say what is quoted — but a reader following contracts.js:845 lands on a closing brace, which corrodes the one property that makes these comments worth their length. Fix: re-anchor by grep-able symbol name rather than by line, or re-derive the numbers now that the parallel files have settled. Second, smaller: transport.bridge.js:65 asserts 'ACCESSORS ARE FUNCTIONS, NEVER SNAPSHOTS — every entry below except collectCdMs / accrualCapH', which `cloud: null` three lines later contradicts; and onClick()'s try has a finally but no catch, so a rejection out of the un-acalled `await b.confirm(...)` escapes as an unhandled rejection, against the header's claim that everything here is wrapped.
